sampling_model.design: A sampled panel \(\varnothing\neq S\in\mathcal P_k\) is chosen ex ante, with \(n_c\in\mathbb N_{>0}\) for every \(c\in S\) and \(\sum_{c\in S}n_c=N\); the \(N\) fixed units are assigned uniformly over the corresponding multi-arm partitions. The panel \(S=\varnothing\) is a separate deterministic population-width case with no assignment law.
sampling_model.units: The covariates \(x_i\) and the full potential-outcome schedule \(Y_i(a,t)\) are fixed; only the assignment \(Z\) is random.
sampling_model.treatment: Assignment to arm \(c\) deploys the deterministic action \(c(x_i)\) at known score \(m_c\).
sampling_model.overlap: For sampled designs, \(S\neq\varnothing\), every selected arm has \(n_c\geq1\), and the in-scope arm counts sum to \(N\); no positive realized arm-by-cell count is required by the Horvitz--Thompson construction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no estimated propensity. Simultaneous without-replacement bounds are constructed for the selected arm-cell means and propagated deterministically through the sharp endpoint maps.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Our bounds are tight, and cannot be improved without further assumptions.
The worst-case regret is approximately equal---and sometimes exactly equal---to the objective function of a k-median problem.
The certificate format is designed with simplicity in mind.
Our approach treats the ILP solver as a black-box oracle.
The proposed confidence intervals for all effect quantiles are simultaneously valid.
The empirical minimax regret estimator is computationally tractable and possesses favorable regret convergence properties.
Our approach relies on constructing averaging estimators where the weights are carefully adapted.
Probability inequalities are obtained for sums of bounded random variables.
There is a combinatorial \(O(\log m+\log k)\)-approximation algorithm for the robust \(k\)-median problem.
Greedily constructed maximum \(k\)-coverage solutions are guaranteed to be within a factor \(1-1/e\) of optimal.

body.tldr: One randomized panel of deterministic machine-learning policies must support sharp causal validation of an entire prespecified update library. With fixed \([0,1]\)-valued potential outcomes, a neutral action, and monotone \(\Gamma\)-Lipschitz finite-population mean responses, two common compatible response schedules attain all lower and upper library endpoints, and two observationally indistinguishable schedules yield an exact prospective width equal to a maximum of weighted nearest matching-score costs. The resulting robust nearest-facility optimization is established combinatorial infrastructure, not the field novelty: a rational mixed-integer representation and an independently checked exhaustive tree implement the causally derived objective. Complete randomization over a nonempty panel with positive arm counts summing to \(N\) gives simultaneous finite-sample assignment-only coverage; the empty panel remains a separate deterministic width-one case.

project_justification.gap: ChenOberst2025 supplies reusable causal validation bounds but not a prospective sharp-width identity for choosing a finite policy panel. AnthonyGoyalGuptaNagarajan2010 already supplies the scenario min-max nearest-facility skeleton, MontielOleaPrallonQiuStoyeSun2025 supplies the closest causal k-median analogy, and HochbaumPathria1998 supplies the zero-sensitivity maximum-coverage boundary.
project_justification.niche: The open field niche is causal rather than combinatorial: derive the exact design loss from observational equivalence of fixed finite-population response schedules while retaining one common pair of endpoint schedules for every future policy.
project_justification.fill: The project proves common sharp endpoint schedules, the attained prospective causal-width identity, and simultaneous randomization-only outer coverage. The mixed-integer program, independently checked exhaustive tree, maximum-coverage reduction, and explicit rational instance are implementation corollaries and falsification infrastructure for those causal results.

body.related_work: Chen and Oberst (2025, Introduction, Section 4, Remark 3.1, and Appendix D.1) establish the reusable-validation model, tight monotonicity bounds, and qualitative multi-model trial guidance; the present field delta is the bounded Lipschitz common-schedule theorem and the exact prospective causal width. Anthony, Goyal, Gupta, and Nagarajan (2010, Section 2 and Theorem 2.2) define robust min-max \(k\)-median and prove a logarithmic approximation. The present action-match exclusions, neutral-action convention, and clipped score costs embed after the metric lift \(\delta=1+d\) into their weighted candidate-restricted scenario nearest-facility skeleton; candidate eligibility, weights, a dummy, and an at-most-\(k\) budget are routine departures, so neither the optimization skeleton nor its approximation theory is claimed as novel. Montiel Olea, Prallon, Qiu, Stoye, and Sun (2025, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.2) connect causal site selection to \(k\)-median for external-validity regret and inform the least-favorable construction, but study a different estimand. Hochbaum and Pathria (1998, abstract and main development) prove the standard greedy guarantee for maximum \(k\)-coverage; at \(\Gamma=0\) the one-future-policy panel problem is exactly weighted maximum coverage. Cheung, Gleixner, and Steffy (2017) and Szeider (2026) provide the general exact rational proof-log foundation, making the branch tree an implementation device rather than a generic certification contribution. Higbee (2025) studies common shape-constrained response curves for new treatments. Caughey, Dafoe, Li, and Miratrix (2023) establish finite-sample randomization-only simultaneous inference for a different causal family, while Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey (2021) study asymptotic adaptive policy evaluation. Hoeffding (1963) supplies the sampling-without-replacement concentration comparison.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The common endpoint schedules establish simultaneous marginal lower and upper corners, not rectangularity of the full joint value set. The facility-location metric lift uses a weighted candidate-restricted variant of the Anthony--Goyal--Gupta--Nagarajan class; it does not transfer their approximation ratio verbatim to every implementation convention. The elementary certificate is complete because exhaustive branching is always available, but its worst-case size is exponential. Its checker must recompute \(\overline W(S^{\star})=v^{\star}\), verify the root and both children of every internal node, and verify every leaf bound; neither \(D^{\star}\) nor global optimality is certificate data. The outer confidence intervals use conservative \(q_x^{-1}\) inflation and are not claimed shortest. Scores, libraries, \(\Gamma\), and the budget are fixed before assignment.
body.honest_scope: The field obligations are the common causal endpoint schedules, the exact prospective width derived from observationally indistinguishable finite-population schedules, and simultaneous assignment-only coverage. The mixed-integer representation, exhaustive certificate, robust \(k\)-median lift, maximum-coverage boundary, and worked instance are supporting propositions. The unresolved first-class question is whether dominance and symmetry yield practical exact certificate generators and polynomial certificate sizes on a meaningful structural class. The proposal does not optimize allocation, estimate future scores, or claim a rectangular joint value set. At \(\Gamma=0\), the width reduces to established weighted unmatched-action coverage.
